name: Compact Anthology of World Literature II: Volumes 4, 5, and 6 (University of North Georgia Press)
goodFor: An anthology of world literature from the seventeenth century to the present, with unit introductions, for a world literature survey course.
attribution: "Compact Anthology of World Literature II: Volumes 4, 5, and 6", by Anita Turlington, Matthew Horton, Karen Dodson, Laura Getty, Kyounghye Kwon and Laura Ng (University of North Georgia Press), linked to https://oer.galileo.usg.edu/english-textbooks/18/; "CC BY-SA 4.0", linked to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; and, when the text shown was shortened or changed, a note that it was.

evidence.quote: This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International License
Texts in the public domain--those published or translated before 1923--are replicated here.
Thus, in Part 6, most of the texts are accessible in the form of links to outside sites.
The UNG Press and the editors of this anthology are looking into issues with links in Volumes 5 and 6.
Each document in ALG Commons is classified by its Creative Commons license.

notes: Checked against the book's own page in the GALILEO Open Learning Materials repository (ALG Commons), which states CC BY-SA 4.0 for the whole work; the repository's FAQ says each document carries its own Creative Commons licence, so the licence is set per book and only this book was read. CC BY-SA allows commercial use; what Ceder changes stays under CC BY-SA 4.0. The page says the anthology reprints only texts published or translated before 1923 (public domain in the US) and links to outside sites for later ones, so in Part 6 (twentieth-century and contemporary literature) most texts are links, not part of the book: what may be shown is the editors' introductions and discussion questions plus the pre-1923 texts, and a linked text is never shown. The page also says (note dated 2022-06-03) the editors were looking into broken links in volumes 5 and 6 and that a revision links to Open Library copies where possible. The repository's FAQ and About pages were read and add no other terms; its footer Copyright link goes to Elsevier's platform terms (not reachable), which were not read. The companion book for World Literature I in the same repository (a different anthology) is CC BY-NC-SA and is in set-aside as ung-world-literature-i.
